text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - Syria has sold Algeria 75,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat for delivery during the next three months. The spokesman for Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade said an agreement was signed on Sunday but did not disclose prices. However, traders said it was close to the western Canadian No.2 red spring wheat price.
The deal was separate from two other tenders which the establishment issued recently for the sale of 100,000 and 50,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat.

WHEAT TENDERS - Morocco will tender on Thursday for 40,000 tonnes optional soft wheat for delivery in first half November, the Office Interprofessionnel des Cereales et Legumineuses said. The closing date for the tender is Thursday at 1530 GMT. It said a lot of 20,000 tonnes will be delivered at Agadir. The two other lots of 10,000 tonnes each are for delivery at the northern ports of Tangier and Nador.

- The CCC said it is retendering for up to 35,000 tonnes U.S. No.2 or better hard red winter, soft white or soft red winter wheat for donation to Eritrea. Shipment was slated for Oct 30-Nov 25, with offers due by October 15.

WHEAT TENDERS (cont.) - Algeria on Monday launched two snap tenders for the purchase of a total of 100,000 tonnes of U.S. and French soft wheat for shipment in November and December, European traders said. It invited traders to submit offers on Monday, valid until Thursday, to supply 50,000 tonnes of wheat in second-half November and the rest in first-half December. Traders said they had been asked to offer both U.S. and French wheat.
- Sri Lanka is to seek on October 18, 100,000 tonnes optional-origin wheat for Nov 11-20 shipment.

WHEAT TENDERS (cont.) - Jordan has postponed a snap tender to buy 150,000 tonnes of U.S. red hard winter or spring wheat or equivalent origin to October 17 due to a U.S. holiday, traders said. Jordan originally set Oct 15 as a deadline for bids, but postponed it due to the U.S. Columbus Day holiday.

- The Cyprus Grain Commission invited tenders for a combined cargo of 12,000 tonnes of U.S. or Canadian spring wheat and 6,000 tonnes of U.S. or Canadian durum wheat. The tender closes October 15 and shipment is November 15-30.
MARKET TALK - Japanese grain traders expressed doubts on Monday that tumbling U.S. corn and soybean futures would spur fresh bouts of buying in the physical markets.

Corn traders said Japanese feed makers had already filled as much as 70 percent of their needs for the first quarter of 1997, although some trade houses were thought to be short in the market in anticipation of further price declines.

...Asian traders also expressed doubts on Monday at reports that China bought hundreds of thousands of tonnes of soybean oil, saying authorities had issued import licenses for only a fraction of that.
